newsitem.title: USA: IPO FOCUS-IPOs show some spark after hibernation.
newsitem.headline: IPO FOCUS-IPOs show some spark after hibernation.

text.p: Demand fueled by money pouring into mutual funds is pushing prices up for some initial public offerings, although the market remains selective.
This week, Kilroy Realty Corp, Administaff Inc and Southwest Bancshares Inc were able to charge higher prices for their newly-minted shares.
Before this week, there had been precious few sightings of recent strength in the IPO market.

Fears about new stocks, with short earnings histories, are being overshadowed as fund managers look for new places to park money, said Zack Shafran, small-cap fund manager for Waddell and Reed. He cited the growing influx of cash into mutual funds in January and the high valuations of blue chip stocks.

"Although the market has broadened out some, people are trying to look away from core blue chips and turning to the IPO market to do that, in hopes of diversifying and finding some new stocks where valuations are a little cheaper," Shafran said.
IPOs on Wednesday also posted strong market debuts, with Kilroy, Administaff, Coldwater Creek Inc and AmerUs Life all reaping premiums of two points or more.
But although the signs are positive, Shafran was cautious about attributing too much significance to them.

"It's still a selective buyers' market. I wouldn't for a moment compare it to spring last year ... And whether it persists remains to be seen, especially with the yield on the long bond approaching seven percent -- that's new competition" for the fund money, he said.
And some weakness persists. Two IPOs that went public today, Photoelectron Corp and Medirisk dipped below their IPO prices in intraday trading.
